title: Video
description: A video, regardless of container format. The bare `media:video` URN matches any video file (mp4, mov, mkv, webm, etc.); format-specific variants like `media:mp4;video` refine it.
documentation:
## Purpose
The umbrella media URN for video content. Caps that operate on any container format (e.g. the generic Extract Frames cap) match on this URN; the planner subsumes more-specific format URNs (`media:mp4;video`, `media:mov;video`, `media:mkv;video`, `media:webm;video`) under it.

## When to use
Use `media:video` when authoring a cap that should accept any supported video container without committing to a specific format. For format-aware pipelines, prefer the per-container URNs so the planner can route correctly without ambiguity.

## Notes
Format-specific variants are produced by the `_video-file.toml` template (one entry per file-type × medium=video). The bare `media:video` URN exists alongside them so caps written against the umbrella have a media spec to anchor to.

## Medium
Medium tags declare the primary human-perceivable nature of a value: visual, audible,
textual, etc. Medium is what a person experiences when consuming the value. Some media
types carry multiple media tags (a PDF is both visual when displayed and textable when
its text layer is extracted).

Medium should not be confused with coercion: `textable` (coercion) means "can be
encoded as UTF-8 text without loss"; `textual` (medium) means "is fundamentally text
to a human reader." A JSON config is textable but not necessarily textual in this
sense — it is structured data that happens to be text-encoded.

The value is a video — a time-sequenced visual stream, typically with synchronised
audio. Caps for video processing, frame extraction, and video transcription match on
this tag.
